Hanoi Urban Noise
Modelling

Measuring noise with smartphones across three contrasting districts, and predicting it from urban form.

01 - Motivation

A public-health problem that Western models were not designed for.

53 dB
WHO ceiling for road-traffic noise
91%
of peak-hour traffic on a Hanoi arterial was two-wheelers (1996-2005)
90-100 dB
horn peaks (Lmax) that averaged metrics smooth away

Models validated on car-centric European cities are unproven on motorcycle-heavy soundscapes. That gap is what we measure.

02 - Study design

Three districts, chosen for contrast - not convenience.

Old quarter

Hoan Kiem Lake

Narrow street canyons, motorcycle-dominated. Sound trapped by facades.

99 measurements
New urban fabric

Ocean Park

Planned high-rise district, car-centric, active construction.

184 measurements
Transport corridor

Vinh Tuy

Major arterial. The densest, fastest-flowing traffic of the three.

80 measurements

20-30 s readings, three cross-calibrated phones, 05:00-23:00. GPS, weather and map context logged automatically.

The most gridlocked sessions were quieter than sparser, faster traffic. Noise tracks speed as much as volume.

05 - Model choice

Two data regimes, two model families.

Fixed sensors

Barcelona

Sensors197, permanent
Samplingcontinuous, 1 min
Structuretime series on a graph
Volumemillions
ModelLSTM, ST-GNN
Mobile survey

Uganda (Sunbird)

Points61,000, one-off
Samplingwalked, spot readings
Structuresparse points
Volume61,000
ModelLightGBM (ours)
Mobile survey

Hanoi (ours)

Points363, one-off
Samplingwalked, 20-30 s, 2 collectors
Structuresparse points
Volume363
ModelLightGBM

A recurrent model needs a sequence at one place. A graph model needs fixed nodes measuring at the same moment. Our points are measured once each, so neither structure exists in our data. Sunbird published the Uganda dataset; the LightGBM model on it is our own extension. Not a claim that one model is better, only that each family needs the data structure it was designed for.

LightGBM on urban form (buildings, roads, intersections, distance to road) plus hour of day.

07 - Key finding

Cross-city transfer fails. Local training doesn't.

A model trained on 61,000 Uganda measurements collapses when applied to Hanoi, and to Barcelona too. What is learned in one city does not travel.

Measured twice, the answer is no. Local data collection cannot be skipped.

08 - Simulation (GAMA), in progress

Turning the map into a scenario tool.

simulation

Work in progress. The predicted map becomes a scenario tool, with moving vehicles whose mix comes from our videos.

LayerStatus
Background level, per hourpredicted (ML)
Traffic volume & mixmeasured (video)
Construction excesscalibrated (+2 dB)
Traffic scenariophysical law
Vehicles as sound sourcesnot identifiable

Sliders: hour of day, traffic volume, construction hours, mitigation. Doubling traffic gives +2.9 dB against +3.0 expected. Per-vehicle emission was not identifiable in our data, so vehicles carry no sound: a documented limit, not an invented number.
